messages:
devin: Quick follow-up on the KV cache RFC — we still need to lock down eviction + sharing invariants before I start the refactor. Main questions: LRU vs LFU vs TTL-first, how aggressive cross-model sharing can be, and what correctness invariants we promise for rollouts.
marta: +1. For rollouts I'm worried about stale KV entries after a model changes its parameterization (eg. quantized variant). We should key on a model fingerprint.
liam: I think we should encode model_id:revision:quantization_tag in the cache key. That avoids cross-variant pollution and keeps lookup O(1).
sasha: Eviction tradeoffs: size-based eviction (memory accounting) + TTL for long-tail prefixes seems good. LRU gives recency which matches prefix reuse; LFU better for very stable prefixes but is heavier.
nora: Also consider segmented-LRU to avoid cache churn from a single hot client (session). We can keep per-shard segments and a probationary queue.
devin: Agreed on key versioning. Two followups: (1) what to do during a canary/model rollback? (2) how to handle prefix caching where we want partial reuse (i.e., reuse KV for first N tokens of a longer prompt).
marta: For rollbacks, if key includes model fingerprint, old entries are simply unused — but we should expire them proactively to free memory. Could run a GC job that scans by prefix model fingerprint.
liam: For partial prefix reuse: store KV at every checkpoint (every K tokens) would allow reuse but increases memory. Alternative: store only the last checkpoint per request and support KV composition by applying delta? Hard.
sasha: Idea: hierarchical prefix keys: key = model_fp + prefix_hash. Also store 'length' in metadata. On request, search for the longest matching stored prefix <= request length. This supports partial reuse without storing every suffix.
nora: That search is O(number_of_prefixes) unless we keep an index. We can maintain a trie per shard keyed by token hashes; memory tradeoff but lookup fast.
devin: We should avoid complex tries in initial refactor. Let's implement longest-prefix-match by keeping a small per-file index mapping from prefix_length -> list of hashes (or a bloom filter) to cheaply check candidates.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Can run background eviction/GC with low priority on dedict nodes.
liam: Eviction algorithm proposal: memory cap per-shard (bytes) + segmented LRU with a probationary segment for new entries. Within limits, prefer evicting entries with low reuse rate (hits / age) and older than min_ttl. If memory pressure then evict by LRU.
sasha: We must ensure correctness for concurrent writes to same key (race if two requests compute KV for same prefix). Use singleflight/dedupe at the shard owner: one in-flight compute and others wait on completion.
marta: Implementation detail: singleflight requires an in-memory wait list per key; need to bound wait list size to avoid mem blowup under storm.
devin: Also think about atomicity of replacement: when we evict, make sure ongoing readers either use snapshot or failover to compute. Atomic CAS on the entry pointer helps.
liam: Pseudocode for dedupe pattern:

```
if get(k) != nil: return
lock_singleflight(k)
if get(k) != nil: unlock; return
val = computeKV(...)
store(k,val)
unlock_singleflight(k)
```

Make sure computeKV has a bounded time and is cancellable.
sasha: Telemetry: record per-prefix hit_count, last_access_ts, size_bytes. Instrument per-shard memory usage and eviction_reason counters (ttl, lru, forced).
nora: Tests: property test for correctness under concurrent compute + eviction. Golden prompts that assert cache hits on repeated calls. Fuzz for race conditions.
devin: What about sharing across tenants? Are we ok sharing KV across customers if model + revision match?
marta: Data sensitivity: KV contains model activations derived from user prompts. Risky to share across tenants in some industries. Default: no cross-tenant sharing unless tenant opt-in. We should support a boolean flag in key namespace: tenant:<id>:... vs public:... .
liam: Adding tenant namespace is trivial in key format. For shared public model endpoints (open prompts) we can set tenant to "public".
sasha: On the infra side, sharding: owner shard should be by key hash (model_fp + tenant namespace). That keeps owner-local singleflight and eviction local.
devin: Rollout plan: implement key-versioning + singleflight + per-shard mem accounting + segmented-LRU. Default: no public sharing until we add audit logs and opt-in.
marta: Action items:
- liam: design key format and include model fingerprint and tenant namespace (ETA 1d)
- sasha: prototype segmented-LRU per-shard and singleflight (ETA 2w)
- nora: tests and property test harness (ETA 2w)
- devin: write RFC follow-up with metrics and rollout plan (ETA 3d)

nora: One more: add metric for "prefix_reuse_ratio" = tokens_served_from_kv / total_tokens to see real impact.
liam: Also track "dedupe_waits" count and average wait latency.
devin: OK. If no objections I'll start the refactor branch tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup!
